title: The Watcher Problem: Why Reality Requires Triadic Unity

canonical_node.axiom: The von Neumann measurement regress admits exactly one structural resolution: a triadic unity of distinct functions (generation, structuration, actualization) operating as a single closed composition.
definitions: Generator G: operator that produces the superposition from the vacuum, G|0> = sum_i c_i |s_i>.
Logos L: operator that establishes the eigenbasis, ordering possibility into intelligible form.
Actualizer A: operator that selects one eigenstate and makes it actual.
Triadic composition T = A  L  G: a single operation with three internal functions, not a chain of observers.
Observation chain: O_{n+1} watches O_n from outside, leading to regress.
Composition: A applies L to G; no element stands outside the operation.
derivation: A single operator cannot be both unitary (generation) and non-unitary (collapse) simultaneously, leading to contradiction.
Two operators (generator and collapser) extend the regress because the collapser itself becomes part of the entangled system requiring further collapse.
Three independent operators require a synchronization function Phi, which constitutes a fourth element, restarting the regress.
No-collapse interpretations (Many-Worlds) abandon the phenomenon of actuality and cannot account for definite experience.
Objective collapse theories insert a termination point by stipulation, begging the question.
The triadic composition T = A  L  G is self-contained: it generates, structures, and actualizes in a single act, terminating the regress.
Removing any function reopens the regress; adding a function adds redundancy. Thus T is the minimal self-contained actualization operation.
canonical_node.action: The system should recognize the triadic composition T = A  L  G as the unique structural resolution to the measurement regress, and apply this structure in modeling actualization events.
boundary: This does not claim to solve the quantum measurement problem empirically or provide a physical mechanism for collapse.
This does not claim that the Trinity was derived from quantum mechanics; it claims a formal isomorphism between the derived structure and Trinitarian theology.
This does not assert that the triadic composition is a physical operator in the standard Hilbert space formalism; it is a structural resolution.
This does not provide experimental predictions or falsifiable tests beyond the logical exhaustion of alternatives.
test: Verify that no single operator can be both unitary and non-unitary in the same respect.
Verify that any two-operator sequence extends the regress by one step.
Verify that any three independent operators require a fourth synchronization function.
Verify that the composition T = A  L  G is closed and does not require an external observer.
Verify that removing any of the three functions reopens the regress.

dg1_dependencies: Von Neumann's formalization of quantum measurement (1932)
Standard Hilbert space formalism of quantum mechanics
Logical exhaustion of structural alternatives (one, two, three operators, no-collapse, collapse-by-fiat)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a formal argument that the measurement regress terminates only in a triadic unity of distinct functions, offering a structural resolution that is claimed to be unique.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the empirical success of quantum mechanics and the mathematical formalism of unitary evolution and projection.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the triadic composition is removed, the measurement regress remains unresolved, and all alternative structural options are claimed to self-defeat.

classification.claim_class: structural resolution to the measurement problem

overstatement_risks: Claims 'precisely one structural resolution' without rigorous proof that all alternatives are exhausted.
Claims formal isomorphism with the Trinity, which may overstate the strength of the correspondence.
Uses theological terms (Logos, Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in a way that may conflate mathematical structure with theological doctrine.
The derivation relies on informal logical arguments rather than a formal proof system.
kill_conditions: If a two-operator or three-independent-operator scheme can be shown to terminate the regress without contradiction, the uniqueness claim fails.
If the triadic composition is shown to be reducible to a two-operator or one-operator scheme without loss, the minimality claim fails.
If the formal exhaustion is incomplete (e.g., missing a viable alternative), the conclusion is unsupported.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the exhaustion of structural options in a proof assistant (e.g., Lean) to verify the uniqueness claim.

plain_summary: This paper argues that the quantum measurement problem's infinite regress of observers can only be resolved by a triadic structure of three distinct functions - generation, structuration, and actualization - unified in a single operation. It claims to formally exhaust all alternatives and finds that only this triadic composition works. The paper then draws a structural parallel to the Christian Trinity. However, the proof is informal and the uniqueness claim is not rigorously established, so the document is classified as not established and recommended for quarantine.
